P_S(q0)=0 ⇔ q0^3-2=1 ⇔ q0=3^{1/3}≈1.44 .
Below q0 the inverse supply is negative and there is no production.  The
textbook producer surplus is therefore the area above the supply curve and
below the price on the feasible interval,

PS=∫_{q0}^{Q*}[P*-P_S(q)]dq
  =P*(Q*-q0)-∫_{q0}^{Q*}ln(q^3-2)dq .

With Simpson/trapezoid
∫_{q0}^{Q*}ln(q^3-2)dq≈9.8–9.9
and P*(Q*-q0)≈4.62×(4.69-1.44)≈15.0,
so
PS≈15.0-9.9≈5.0–5.3,
≈5.1 on the 4.69/4.62 root.

Hence the net surplus created by the trade is
W=CS+PS
 =I_D(Q*)-P*Q0-∫_{q0}^{Q*}P_S(q)dq
 =∫_0^{Q*}P_D(q)dq-P*Q0-∫_{q0}^{Q*}P_S(q)dq
 ≈32.5-6.7-9.9≈15–17,
about 15.9 with the Simpson numbers quoted above, CS≈10.8 and PS≈5.1.

That is the area between demand and the economically relevant part of
supply up to Q*.  The P*Q0≈6.6–6.7 term is a pure transfer from consumers
to producers and is conventionally removed when the surplus is written as
CS+PS with PS measured from the zero-price choke point q0=3^{1/3}.  The
≈22–23 figures that appear in the room are I_D-∫_{q0}^{Q*}P_S, i.e.
CS+PS+P*Q0, and therefore overstate net welfare by the inessential
transfer P*Q0.  On the proper zero-price normalisation the competitive
total surplus at Q*≈4.69, P*≈4.62 is the ≈15–17 units quoted above,
≈15.9 in the present discretisation, with the strict between-the-curves
integral on [q0,Q*] being ≈7–8.

3.text:
Inverse supply and inverse demand are

* $P_{S}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)$ ,  $Q^{3}>2$ ,
* $P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}>0$ .

On a competitive market

$$P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},\qquad Q^{*}>2^{1/3}$$
is monotone on the admissible branch and has the unique real root

$$f(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0
\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad 
Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\;, $$

in the usual numerical work

$$Q^{*}\approx 4.69\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.62 ,
\qquad P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 21.6\!-\!21.7 .$$

Put

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq
      =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq,\qquad 
I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq ,
\qquad q_{a}=2^{1/3}, $$
i.e. the finite part of the inverse supply on its real domain.
In the $u=\arctan q$ variable

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du, $$

which is non-elementary and is evaluated numerically.  With the root
above

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 3.24\!-\!3.28\times10^{1}\approx 32.5, $$

and

$$\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
     \;\approx\;9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 9.7\!-\!9.9 , $$

so that on the $0\to Q^{*}$ Marshallian convention

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0,$$
$$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx11.7\!-\!12.0,$$
and the $CS+PS$ surplus

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-
      \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq $$
is

$$W^{*}\approx 32.5-9.7\approx 22\!-\!23, $$

e.g. $I_{D}\approx32.47$, $I_{S}\approx9.70$ and $W^{*}\approx22.8$,
$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS^{*}\approx12.0$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$ on the
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root.  In closed form

$$W^{*}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
       \int_{2^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq,
\qquad \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}, $$

which is the conventional net area between inverse demand and inverse
supply up to the market clearing point.

Remark on normalisation.  The economically meaningful zero-price choke
of the inverse supply is $P_{S}(Q_{0})=0$, $Q_{0}^{3}=3$,
$Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.  With the usual textbook $PS_{0}$ measured
from $Q_{0}$,

$$PS_{0}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq,
\qquad 
W_{0}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}
    =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq,$$

i.e. $W_{0}=W^{*}-P^{*}Q_{0}$.  Numerically

$$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx9.8\!-\!9.9,\qquad 
P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.66,$$

so that

$$CS^{*}\approx10.8,\qquad PS_{0}\approx5.0\!-\!5.3,\qquad
W_{0}\approx15\!-\!17, $$

about $W_{0}\simeq15.9$ with $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.
The $ \approx22\!-\!23$ figure above is the $I_{D}-I_{S}$ $CS+PS$
value quoted in the literature; the $ \approx15\!-\!16$ figure is the
same quantity with the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ transfer removed, i.e. the surplus
measured from the economic zero-price point $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$. ∎

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the group on the equilibrium itself. The clearing condition 
$\ln(Q^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is monotone for $Q^{3}>2$ and

* $f(4.68)=-8\times10^{-3}$,
* $f(4.70)=+8\times10^{-3}$,

so that

$Q^{*}\simeq 4.69\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.62$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$,

is essentially universal. The dispute is the accounting of the surplus, not the root.

On the inverse side the economically relevant supply is the part with
$P_{S}(Q)\ge0$.  $P_{S}(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$,

$Q_{0}= \sqrt[3]{3}\approx1.44$,

whereas $Q_{a}=\sqrt[3]{2}\approx1.26$ is only the mathematical branch point
of the log.  Producer surplus is conventionally

$PS(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
        =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$ ,

and consumer surplus is

$CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$ .

Hence the textbook $CS+PS$ is

$W^{*}=CS+PS
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q_{0}
       -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$ ,

i.e. the integral of demand up to $Q^{*}$ minus the economic area under
marginal cost up to $Q^{*}$ with the fixed transfer $P^{*}Q_{0}$ removed.

Numerically

$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 32.4\!-\!32.6$,

$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx 9.8\!-\!9.9$,

$P^{*}Q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66$,

so that

$CS\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}
   \approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9$,

$PS\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}
   \approx15.0-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$,

and

$W^{*}=CS+PS
      \approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}
      \approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!17$,

about $W^{*}\simeq15.9$ with the Simpson numbers usually quoted,
$CS\simeq10.8$, $PS\simeq5.1$, $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.
That is the net area between $P_{D}$ and $P_{S}$ on the economically
feasible interval $Q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$ plus the usual consumer surplus
below $Q_{0}$.

The $\approx22\!-\!23$ figures that appear as $I_{d}-I_{s}$,
$I_{d}=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}$, $I_{s}=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$, are
$W^{*}+P^{*}Q_{0}$.  They keep the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.7$ fixed transfer
in the total.  If the supply integral is started at the mathematical
branch point $Q_{a}=\sqrt[3]{2}$ the producer integral is taken over a
region where $P_{S}<0$, i.e. over a price where the firm would be paid
to produce, and the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ term is double-counted.  Removing that
transfer gives the conventional net welfare $\approx15\!-\!16$, essentially

so that

     =\ln\!\big(Q^{*3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.7,

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 4.62\times4.69\approx 21.6\!-\!21.7 .$$

Put

$$I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq ,\qquad

$$I_{d}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du
\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8\approx 32.5, $$

and

$$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq
\approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 9.7 ,$$

 =q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-

Hence on the usual $CS+PS$ book-keeping

$$ PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx 21.7-9.7\approx 11.8\!-\!12.0,
 $$

and the net Marshallian surplus at the competitive point is

      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5,$$
$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9,$$

with $Q_{0}$ the economic zero-price choke of the inverse supply.

The subtle point is the origin of producer surplus.  $P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is real for $q>\root3\of2$ but it is economically negative for
$\root3\of2<q<\root3\of3$,

$$P_{S}(q)=0\iff q^{3}-2=1\iff Q_{0}=\root3\of3\approx1.442 .$$

Producer surplus is the area under the market price and above the
marginal cost curve on the actually producible part of the schedule,
i.e.

$$PS(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
        =P^{*}\big(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\big)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq ,$$

and

$$CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}.$$

Hence on the economically feasible domain

$$W^{*} =CS+PS
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq .$$

The $P^{*}Q_{0}$ rectangle is the transfer that is normally removed
when surplus is written as the net area between the two curves.  With
$Q_{0}=\root3\of3$,

$$P^{*}Q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66,$$

$$CS\approx I_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.8,$$
$$PS\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-I_{S}\approx4.62\times3.25-9.9\approx5.1,$$

so that

$$W^{*}=CS+PS\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-P^{*}Q_{0}-I_{S}
      \approx32.5-6.7-9.9\approx15.9, $$

about $15\!-\!17$ monetary units, $CS\approx10.8$ and $PS\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$
on the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ equilibrium.  This is the
usual net area between $P_{D}$ and $P_{S}$ on the feasible interval
$Q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$ and the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ term is the conventional
book-keeping correction that removes the artificial surplus generated
on the $0\to Q_{0}$ part of the supply schedule where the inverse supply
is negative.  Up to quadrature the value is $W^{*}\simeq15.9$, essentially
the $\sim16$ total surplus quoted for the competitive equilibrium.

19.text:
The inverse schedules are

$$P_{s}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right),\qquad 
P_{d}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2 , $$

and on the competitive market

$$P_{s}(Q^{*})=P_{d}(Q^{*})\iff 
f(Q):=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0 , $$

$f$ is strictly increasing on $Q>\root3\!\of2$.  Numerically

* $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$,
* $Q^{*}=4.68\!-\!4.70$,

in practice

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}
      \simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7\approx 4.62 ,
$$

$P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq 21.6\!-\!21.7$.  On the usual Marshallian
normalisation

\begin{equation*}
CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq,
\end{equation*}

$Q_{0}=\root3\!\of3$ being the economic zero of the log supply,
$P_{s}(Q_{0})=0$, so that with the admissible mathematical lower
limit $q_{a}=\root3\!\of2$

\begin{equation*}
I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
          \approx 3.24\!-\!3.29\times10^{1}\approx 32.5 ,
\end{equation*}

and, with the elementary anti-derivative of $\ln(q^{3}-2)$,

\begin{equation*}
I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
          \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 9.7 ,
\end{equation*}

on the usual $q_{a}=\root3\!\of2$ domain.  Hence on the textbook
$CS+PS$ bookkeeping

* $CS^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!11.0$,
  $\approx10.8$,
* $PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}\approx 21.7-9.7\approx 11.8\!-\!12.0$,

and

\begin{equation*}
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-
      \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
     \approx 32.5-9.7\approx 2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1},
\end{equation*}

i.e. $W^{*}\simeq22\!-\!23$ welfare units, $W^{*}\approx22.6\!-\!22.9$
for the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root, the familiar
$CS\approx\$10.8$, $PS\approx\$11.8$ decomposition with $P^{*}Q^{*}
\approx\$21.7$ of gross trade value.

With the strict economic zero-price normalisation
$P_{s}(Q_{0})=0$, $Q_{0}=\root3\!\of3\approx1.44$,

$$PS_{e}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s},
\qquad 
W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}
    =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dq-P^{*}Q_{0}
     -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq ,$$

which removes the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.7$ transfer.  Numerically

$\displaystyle\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}\approx9.8\!-\!10.0$,

$PS_{e}\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$ and

$W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}\approx10.8+5.1\approx15\!-\!17$, about
$W_{e}\simeq15.9$ with $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, the
$ \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}[P_{d}-P_{s}]dq\approx7.3\!-\!7.5$ net area
between the two curves on the economically feasible interval
$Q_{0}\le Q\le Q^{*}$.  This is the $CS\approx10.8$, $PS\approx5.1$,
$W\approx15\!-\!16$ zero-price normalisation quoted in Colleagues 1,
11, 19.  Up to the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ transfer this is the $W^{*}\approx
22\!-\!23$ $CS+PS$ value above.

8.text:
The inverse schedules can be written on the admissible branch

$P_{s}(q)=\ln \!\big(q^{3}-2\big) ,\qquad q>q_{a},\qquad 
q_{a}=2^{1/3}$,
$P_{d}(q)=18\,e^{-\arctan q}$ ,
$P_{s}(q)$ is strictly increasing on $q>q_{a}$ and $P_{d}$ is strictly
decreasing, so that

\begin{equation*}
P_{s}(Q^{*})=P_{d}(Q^{*}),\qquad 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}} ,
\end{equation*}
has a unique real root on $q>q_{a}$.  On $4<Q<5$

$f(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ changes sign
between $4.68$ and $4.70$ and

\begin{equation*}
Q^{*}\approx 4.69\!-\!4.70,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx
4.6\!-\!4.7,
\end{equation*}
e.g. $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq21.6\!-\!21.7$,
is the competitive price quantity pair.  In the $u=\arctan q$
variable

$I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq
   =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du$, $u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}$,
so that numerically

$I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx
3.24\!-\!3.29\times10^{1}\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8$,

say $I_{d}\approx 32.5$.  On the admissible supply branch

$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq$,
$q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.26$, is finite and

$I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx9.7\!-\!9.9$,

e.g. $I_{s}\approx9.70$ for $Q^{*}\approx4.69$.  With the usual
Marshallian accounting

$CS^{*}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}$,
$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}(Q^{*})$,

hence

$CS^{*}\approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!11.0\approx \$10.8$,

$PS^{*}\approx 21.7-9.7\approx 11.8\!-\!12.0\approx \$12.0$,

and the net $CS+PS$ surplus on the admissible branch is

\begin{equation*}
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-
      \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq\approx 22\!-\!23,
\end{equation*}
about $W^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$ with the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$ root, e.g. $W^{*}\approx22.8$, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$,
$PS^{*}\approx12.0$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.  This is the
$I_{d}-I_{s}$ total surplus $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{d}-P_{s}]_{+}dq$
normally quoted as the competitive total welfare.

Remark.  If the producer surplus is normalised to the economic
zero-price point $P_{s}(Q_{0})=0$, $Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx
1.442$, the economically relevant producer surplus is
$PS_{0}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$
and

$W_{0}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}
      -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq\approx15\!-\!17$,

about $W_{0}\simeq15.9$, $CS^{*}\simeq10.8$, $PS_{0}\simeq5.1$,
the textbook $CS+PS$ with the $P_{s}=0$ origin.  The $\approx6\!-\!7$
difference between $W^{*}$ and $W_{0}$ is the $P^{*}Q_{0}
+\int_{q_{a}}^{Q_{0}}P_{s}dq$ shift between the mathematical domain
normalisation $q_{a}=2^{1/3}$ and the economic zero-price
normalisation $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$.  The equilibrium $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$ is robust under either convention.

12.text:
The market clearing price is the unique real solution of

$$P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff 
\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv f(Q)=0,\qquad 
Q^{3}>2 ,$$

$f$ is strictly monotone on $Q>\root3\of2$ and

* $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$,

so that on the usual numerical accuracy

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69 ,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7, $$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.689$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ and $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$.
Put $Q_{0}$ for the economic zero of the inverse supply,
$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=\root3\of3\approx1.442$, and
on the admissible branch $q\ge Q_{0}$

$$ 
{\rm CS}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},
\qquad 
{\rm PS}(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq ,
$$

so that with the inessential $P^{*}Q_{0}$ cancellation

$$ 
W(Q^{*})={\rm CS}+{\rm PS}
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
       =I_{d}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*}) .
$$

In the $u=\arctan q$ variable

$$I_{d}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
           =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du ,$$

and with the root above

$$I_{d}(Q^{*})\approx 3.24\!-\!3.29\times10^{1}\approx32.4\!-\!32.8,
\qquad I_{d}\approx32.5,$$

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.7,$$
hence

$${\rm CS}^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8,$$

and

$$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
          \approx9.8\!-\!9.9\approx9.9, $$

so that on the conventional $0\to Q^{*}$ Marshallian convention

$${\rm PS}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8\!-\!12.0,$$

and

$$W^{*}= {\rm CS}^{*}+{\rm PS}^{*}=I_{d}-I_{s}
      \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23, $$

e.g. $W^{*}\approx22.6$ with $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,
${\rm CS}^{*}\approx10.8$, ${\rm PS}^{*}\approx11.8$ and $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.
With the coarse Simpson rule used in the discussion this is the
$W^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$ total Marshallian surplus,
$I_{d}\approx32.5$ gross willingness to pay, generated at the
$Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$ competitive equilibrium.

Remark on normalisation.  On the textbook zero-price normalisation

$${\rm PS}_{0}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S},
\qquad 
W_{0}={\rm CS}+{\rm PS}_{0}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq,
$$

so that $ {\rm PS}_{0}\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$ and
$W_{0}\approx15\!-\!17$, about $W_{0}\approx15.9$ with the same
$Q^{*},P^{*}$, i.e. the $CS\approx10.8$, $PS_{0}\approx5.1$,
$W_{0}\approx15.9$ figure often quoted as the between-the-curves
net surplus.  The $I_{d}-I_{s}\approx22\!-\!23$ number above is the
$CS+PS$ surplus with the usual $P^{*}Q^{*}$ cancellation.

public_text.6:
The competitive price is obtained from the inverse schedules

$$P_{S}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right),\qquad 
P_{D}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2 ,
$$

$$P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})\iff 
f(Q):=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0  .
$$

$f$ is monotone on $Q>\root3\of2$ and

$f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$,

so that on the admissible branch

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\approx 4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}=\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7,
$$

e.g.

$$Q^{*}\approx4.69,\qquad P^{*}\approx4.62,\qquad 
P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 21.6\!-\!21.7 .$$

Put 
$I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq$ and 
$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$ with $Q_{a}=2^{1/3}$ the
mathematical start of the log–supply.  With $u=\arctan q$

$$I_{d}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
           =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du
           \approx 32.4\!-\!32.8\approx 32.5 ,$$

and, in closed form,

$$\int\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
=q\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)-3q-\!\int\!\frac{6q^{2}}{q^{3}-2}dq,
$$

so that on the real domain

$$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
          \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 9.7 .
$$

On the usual $CS+PS$ convention

\begin{align*}
CS^{*}&=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}
      =I_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0,\\
PS^{*}&=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
      =P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx11.8\!-\!12.2,
\end{align*}

and the net Marshallian surplus at the clearing point is

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =I_{d}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
     \approx 32.5-9.7\approx 22\!-\!23,
$$

e.g. $W^{*}\simeq 22.6\!-\!22.9$, $CS^{*}\simeq10.8$ and
$PS^{*}\simeq12.0$ for the $Q^{*}\!\approx\!4.69$, $P^{*}\!\approx\!4.62$
root.  In round numbers $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx\$4.6$,
$CS\approx\$10.8$, $PS\approx\$11\!-\!12$ and $CS+PS\approx\$22\!-\!23$
of total surplus is created at the competitive equilibrium.

Remark.  With the economic zero-price normalisation
$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44$, the
conventional textbook producer surplus is 
$PS_{0}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$
and $W_{0}=CS+PS_{0}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}
-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq\approx15\!-\!17$, about $15.9$ with the
Simpson numbers above, i.e. the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ transfer removed from the
$I_{d}-I_{s}$ figure quoted above.
public_text.5:
The equilibrium itself is settled. 
$P_S(Q)=\ln(Q^3-2)$, $P_D(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ and

$\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$

has the unique real root on $Q^3>2$

$Q^{*}\simeq 4.69\!-\!4.70$,  $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}
\simeq4.62\!-\!4.64$,

$P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq21.6\!-\!21.7$, and

$I_d(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\simeq32.4\!-\!32.8$

is robust for Simpson/trapezoid. That part is not in dispute.

The disagreement is the economic definition of the producer surplus.
$P_S(q)=\ln(q^3-2)$ is negative on $2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$ and $P_S(q)=0$
iff $q_0^3-2=1$,

$q_0=\sqrt[3]{3}\simeq1.442$,

the usual economic choke point.  Producer surplus is the area above the
marginal cost curve and below $P^{*}$ *on the economically feasible set*,
i.e.

$PS =\int_{q_0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P^{*}-P_S(q)\big]dq
    =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-q_0\right)-\int_{q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S(q)dq$,

and

$CS =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$.

Hence the textbook net surplus is

$W=CS+PS
  =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_D(q)dq-P^{*}q_0-\int_{q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S(q)dq
  =I_d(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_0-I_s(Q^{*})$,

with $I_s(Q^{*})=\int_{q_0}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^3-2)dq\simeq9.8\!-\!9.9$.

Numerically $P^{*}q_0\simeq4.62\times1.442\simeq6.66\!-\!6.70$, 
$I_d\simeq32.5$, $I_s\simeq9.87$, so that

$CS\simeq I_d-P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq32.5-21.7\simeq10.7\!-\!10.9$,

$PS\simeq P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_0)-I_s\simeq15.0-9.9\simeq5.0\!-\!5.4$,

and

$W=CS+PS\simeq I_d-P^{*}q_0-I_s\simeq32.5-6.7-9.9\simeq15.9$,

about $15\!-\!17$ monetary units, $16$ in round numbers, for the
$Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$ equilibrium.

The $I_d-I_s\simeq22\!-\!23$ numbers quoted by several colleagues are
$I_d-\int_{q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S$, i.e. $CS+PS+P^{*}q_0$.  The $P^{*}q_0$
rectangle is a pure transfer from consumers to producers and is not
created surplus.  Counting it as producer surplus is the same as taking
$PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S$, which adds the inframarginal
rectangle $P^{*}q_0$ to the true economic producer surplus and inflates
welfare by $\approx6.6\!-\!6.7$ units.  Once the surplus is measured from
the zero-price choke point $q_0=\sqrt[3]{3}$, the conventional
$CS+PS$ total is the $\approx15.9$ net area between demand and supply up
to $Q^{*}$, the $\approx10.8$ consumer surplus plus the $\approx5.1$
genuine producer surplus normally quoted in the textbook definition.
public_text.2:
I agree with the numerical core that is converging in the room. The market clearing

ln(Q³-2)=18 e^{-arctan Q}

is monotone for Q>∛2 and the root is

Q*≈4.68–4.70,  about Q*≈4.69,
P* = ln(Q*³-2)=18 e^{-arctan Q*}≈4.62,

P*Q*≈21.6–21.7, and

I_d(Q*) = ∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{-arctan q} dq ≈ 32.4–32.5,

is essentially common to all of us now, e.g. 32.45–32.48 with the usual Simpson/ sec² quadrature. Consumer surplus

CS = I_d - P*Q* ≈ 32.45 - 21.67 ≈ 10.7–10.9

is therefore settled at ≈ $10.8.

Where the welfare number splits is the economic lower limit for producer surplus. Inverse supply is

P_S(q)=ln(q³-2),   P_S(q)=0 ⇔ q³-2=1 ⇔ q0=∛3≈1.442.

For ∛2<q<∛3 the mathematical log is negative, i.e. P_S<0. A producer will not supply at a negative price; the economically feasible branch of the supply is P_S≥0, q≥q0. The textbook Marshallian producer surplus is therefore

PS = ∫_{q0}^{Q*} [P* - P_S(q)] dq
   = P*(Q* - q0) - ∫_{q0}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq .

With the root above

∫_{q0}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq ≈ 9.8–9.9,

say ≈9.87, and P*(Q*-q0)≈4.62×(4.69-1.442)≈14.98, so

PS≈14.98-9.87≈5.1–5.3.

Hence the conventional CS+PS total, with the zero-price choke point removed,

W = CS + PS
  = I_d(Q*) - P* q0 - ∫_{q0}^{Q*} P_S(q) dq
  ≈ 32.45 - 4.62×1.442 - 9.87
  ≈ 32.45 - 6.67 - 9.87
  ≈ 15.9–16.0

in the same units, ≈ $10.8 consumer surplus and ≈ $5.1 producer surplus. That is the 15–17 total quoted by colleagues 1, 11 and 19, and it is the usual textbook CS+PS normalisation: the P*Q0≈6.7 transfer that remains if the supply integral is started at the mathematical domain start q_a=∛2 is an accounting artefact and is normally removed by measuring producer surplus from P_S=0.

If the integral is kept on the purely mathematical domain q_a=∛2 the “between the curves’’ area ∫_{q0}^{Q*} [P_D-P_S] dq is ≈7.3–8.9 and the un-normalised I_d - I_s is ≈22–23, which is the 22.5–22.9 figure several of us are reporting. The 22–23 number is I_d - ∫_{q_a}^{Q*} P_S, i.e. CS+PS with the P*Q0 shift retained. Economically the sensible welfare measure is the zero-price normalised one, about 15.9 with Q*≈4.69, P*≈4.62, CS≈10.8, PS≈5.1.
public_text.9:
I think we all agree on the mechanical part now. The clearing condition

ln(Q³-2)=18 e^{-arctan Q}

has the unique interior root

Q*≈4.69–4.70,   P* = ln(Q*³-2)=18 e^{-arctan Q*}≈4.62

so P*Q*≈21.7 and ∫₀^{Q*} P_D≈32.4–32.8 is a stable number.

Where the disagreement is really about the book-keeping of producer surplus, not about the root.

P_S(Q)=ln(Q³-2) is economically meaningful only from its zero-price choke. 
P_S(Q0)=0 ⇔ Q0³-2=1 ⇔ Q0=∛3≈1.44.  That is the point where marginal cost is zero, i.e. where production would start in a textbook inverse-supply story.  The mathematical domain Q>∛2≈1.26 is a log singularity, not an economic origin.

With the conventional Marshallian definitions

CS = ∫₀^{Q*} P_D(q)dq - P*Q*,
PS = ∫_{Q0}^{Q*} [P* - P_S(q)]dq = P*(Q*-Q0) - ∫_{Q0}^{Q*} P_S(q)dq

the P*Q0 rectangle is not created surplus, it is the infra-marginal transfer that is normally removed when we sum CS+PS.  Then

Inverse supply and inverse demand are

* $P_{S}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)$ ,  $Q^{3}>2$ ,
* $P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}>0$ .

On a competitive market

$$P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},\qquad Q^{*}>2^{1/3}$$
is monotone on the admissible branch and has the unique real root

$$f(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0
\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad 
Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\;, $$

in the usual numerical work

$$Q^{*}\approx 4.69\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.62 ,
\qquad P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 21.6\!-\!21.7 .$$

Put

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq
      =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq,\qquad 
I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq ,
\qquad q_{a}=2^{1/3}, $$
i.e. the finite part of the inverse supply on its real domain.
In the $u=\arctan q$ variable

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du, $$

which is non-elementary and is evaluated numerically.  With the root
above

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 3.24\!-\!3.28\times10^{1}\approx 32.5, $$

and

$$\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
     \;\approx\;9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 9.7\!-\!9.9 , $$

so that on the $0\to Q^{*}$ Marshallian convention

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0,$$
$$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx11.7\!-\!12.0,$$
and the $CS+PS$ surplus

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-
      \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq $$
is

$$W^{*}\approx 32.5-9.7\approx 22\!-\!23, $$

e.g. $I_{D}\approx32.47$, $I_{S}\approx9.70$ and $W^{*}\approx22.8$,
$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS^{*}\approx12.0$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$ on the
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root.  In closed form

$$W^{*}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
       \int_{2^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq,
\qquad \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}, $$

which is the conventional net area between inverse demand and inverse
supply up to the market clearing point.

Remark on normalisation.  The economically meaningful zero-price choke
of the inverse supply is $P_{S}(Q_{0})=0$, $Q_{0}^{3}=3$,
$Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.  With the usual textbook $PS_{0}$ measured
from $Q_{0}$,

$$PS_{0}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq,
\qquad 
W_{0}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}
    =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq,$$

i.e. $W_{0}=W^{*}-P^{*}Q_{0}$.  Numerically

$$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx9.8\!-\!9.9,\qquad 
P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.66,$$

so that

$$CS^{*}\approx10.8,\qquad PS_{0}\approx5.0\!-\!5.3,\qquad
W_{0}\approx15\!-\!17, $$

about $W_{0}\simeq15.9$ with $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.
The $ \approx22\!-\!23$ figure above is the $I_{D}-I_{S}$ $CS+PS$
value quoted in the literature; the $ \approx15\!-\!16$ figure is the
same quantity with the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ transfer removed, i.e. the surplus
measured from the economic zero-price point $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$. ∎
public_text.13:
I agree with the group on the equilibrium itself. The clearing condition 
$\ln(Q^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is monotone for $Q^{3}>2$ and

* $f(4.68)=-8\times10^{-3}$,
* $f(4.70)=+8\times10^{-3}$,

so that

$Q^{*}\simeq 4.69\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.62$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$,

is essentially universal. The dispute is the accounting of the surplus, not the root.

On the inverse side the economically relevant supply is the part with
$P_{S}(Q)\ge0$.  $P_{S}(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$,

$Q_{0}= \sqrt[3]{3}\approx1.44$,

whereas $Q_{a}=\sqrt[3]{2}\approx1.26$ is only the mathematical branch point
of the log.  Producer surplus is conventionally

$PS(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
        =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$ ,

and consumer surplus is

$CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$ .

Hence the textbook $CS+PS$ is

$W^{*}=CS+PS
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q_{0}
       -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$ ,

i.e. the integral of demand up to $Q^{*}$ minus the economic area under
marginal cost up to $Q^{*}$ with the fixed transfer $P^{*}Q_{0}$ removed.

Numerically

$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 32.4\!-\!32.6$,

$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx 9.8\!-\!9.9$,

$P^{*}Q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66$,

so that

$CS\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}
   \approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9$,

$PS\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}
   \approx15.0-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$,

and

$W^{*}=CS+PS
      \approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}
      \approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!17$,

about $W^{*}\simeq15.9$ with the Simpson numbers usually quoted,
$CS\simeq10.8$, $PS\simeq5.1$, $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.
That is the net area between $P_{D}$ and $P_{S}$ on the economically
feasible interval $Q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$ plus the usual consumer surplus
below $Q_{0}$.

The $\approx22\!-\!23$ figures that appear as $I_{d}-I_{s}$,
$I_{d}=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}$, $I_{s}=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$, are
$W^{*}+P^{*}Q_{0}$.  They keep the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.7$ fixed transfer
in the total.  If the supply integral is started at the mathematical
branch point $Q_{a}=\sqrt[3]{2}$ the producer integral is taken over a
region where $P_{S}<0$, i.e. over a price where the firm would be paid
to produce, and the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ term is double-counted.  Removing that
transfer gives the conventional net welfare $\approx15\!-\!16$, essentially
the $\sim15.9$ total surplus normally quoted for the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$ competitive equilibrium.
public_text.18:
Market clearing is

$$P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff \ln\!\big(Q^{3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv f(Q)=0,
\qquad Q>\root3\of2 ,$$

$f$ is strictly increasing on the admissible branch and

* $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$

so that

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\approx 4.69\;, $$

$$P^{*}=P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})
     =\ln\!\big(Q^{*3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.7,
\qquad P^{*}\approx4.62, $$

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 4.62\times4.69\approx 21.6\!-\!21.7 .$$

Put

$$I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq ,\qquad 
I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq,
\qquad q_{a}=\root3\of2 .$$

With $u=\arctan q$

$$I_{d}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du
\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8\approx 32.5, $$

and

$$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq
\approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 9.7 ,$$

the integral being elementary,
$\int\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
 =q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-
 \int\!\frac{6q^{2}}{q^{3}-2}dq$.
Hence on the usual $CS+PS$ book-keeping

$$ CS^{*}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!11.0,
\approx \$10.8, $$

$$ PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx 21.7-9.7\approx 11.8\!-\!12.0,
 $$

and the net Marshallian surplus at the competitive point is

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*})
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
      \approx 32.5-9.7\approx 2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}, $$

e.g. $W^{*}\simeq 22.6\!-\!22.9$, $W^{*}\approx22.8$ for
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.  In closed form

$$W^{*}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
\int_{\root3\of2}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq,\qquad
\ln\!\big(Q^{*3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},$$

which is $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ and $PS^{*}\approx12.0$ for the
$Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ competitive equilibrium.

Remark on the zero-price normalisation.  The economic zero of the
inverse supply is $P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=\root3\of3
\approx1.442$.  With the textbook producer surplus
$PS_{e}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}[P^{*}-P_{S}(q)]dq$ the transfer
$P^{*}Q_{0}$ is removed and

$$W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}
      =I_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-I_{s}^{0}(Q^{*})
      \approx15\!-\!17, $$

about $CS\approx10.8$, $PS_{e}\approx5.1$ and $W_{e}\approx15.9$ on the
same $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root.  The $ \approx22\!-\!23$
figure above is the conventional $I_{d}-I_{s}$ $CS+PS$ value with the
formal lower limit $q_{a}=\root3\of2$ for the inverse supply; it
coincides with $W_{e}+P^{*}Q_{0}$.  This is the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$ competitive outcome quoted in the literature.
public_text.11:
The clearing price is the unique real solution of

$$P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff 
\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2,
$$

and $f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is strictly increasing on
$Q>\sqrt[3]{2}$.  Numerically

* $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$,

so that with the usual Newton / bisection

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\approx 4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7, $$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx 4.69$ and $P^{*}\approx 4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 21.6\!-\!21.7$.

On the inverse notation

$$
CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq,
$$

$a=\sqrt[3]{2}$ being the mathematical start of the log–supply,
and

$$
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}= 
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq .
$$

Putting $t=\arctan q$,

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
      =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
      \approx 32.4\!-\!32.8\approx 32.5, $$

and with $a=2^{1/3}$

$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
      \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 9.7, $$

so that on the $0\to Q^{*}$ normalisation

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!11.0,
$$

$$
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}\approx 21.7-9.7\approx 11.8\!-\!12.0,
$$

and

$$
W^{*}=I_{D}-I_{S}\approx 32.5-9.7\approx 22\!-\!23,
$$

e.g. $CS^{*}\!\approx\!10.8$, $PS^{*}\!\approx\!11.8\!-\!12.0$,
$W^{*}\!\approx\!22.6\!-\!22.9$ for the quoted root
$Q^{*}\!\approx\!4.69$, $P^{*}\!\approx\!4.62$.  In particular

$W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq\approx22.5\!-\!23.0$,

the familiar $CS+PS$ decomposition of the competitive surplus at the
marginal-benefit = marginal-cost point.

Remark on the zero–price normalisation.  With the economic choke
$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0$, $Q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}\approx1.44$, the producer surplus
normally quoted as $PS_{0}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$
is $PS_{0}\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$ and

$$W_{0}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq
      \approx15\!-\!17,$$

about $15.9$ with the same quadrature, i.e. the $CS\approx10.8$,
$PS_{0}\approx5.1$, $W_{0}\approx15.9$ textbook $CS+PS$ figure.  The
$ \approx22\!-\!23$ number above is the $I_{D}-I_{S}$ net surplus on the
mathematical domain $q>a$ and is the $CS+PS$ value most of the group is
quoting.
public_text.15:
The competitive clearing price is the (unique) real solution of

$$P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q),\qquad 
P_{S}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right),\;\;
P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2, $$

i.e.

$$f(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0 .$$

$f$ is strictly increasing on the admissible branch.  $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$
and Newton iteration gives

* $Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
* $P^{*}=P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})=\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)
       =18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7$,

$P^{*}\approx4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$ in the units of the
two curves.  This is the market clearing pair.

Put

$$I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq
           =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq ,\qquad 
I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq, $$

with the first economically feasible point $P_{S}(q_{0})=0$, 
$q_{0}^{3}=3$, $q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.44$, $q_{a}=2^{1/3}\simeq1.26$ the
mathematical branch point.  On the usual $0\to Q^{*}$ normalisation

$$ {\rm CS}(Q^{*})=I_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad 
 {\rm PS}^{*}(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}(Q^{*}), $$

so that

$$W^{*}= {\rm CS}^{*}+{\rm PS}^{*}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*}).$$

Numerically

$$I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx
3.24\!-\!3.28\times10^{1}\approx32.4\!-\!32.8, $$

about $I_{d}\simeq32.5$ for $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, and

$$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
        \approx9.7\!-\!10.0,$$

$I_{s}\simeq9.8\!-\!9.9$ with the $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ zero-price truncation,
$I_{s}\simeq9.6\!-\!9.7$ on the mathematical branch $q_{a}=2^{1/3}$.
Hence

$${\rm CS}^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0,$$
$${\rm PS}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}\approx21.7-9.8\approx11.8\!-\!12.0,$$

and in the conventional $CS+PS$ book-keeping

$$W^{*}= I_{d}-I_{s}\approx32.5-9.8\approx22\!-\!23,$$

e.g.

$$Q^{*}\approx4.69,\qquad P^{*}\approx4.62,\qquad 
{\rm CS}^{*}\approx10.8,\qquad {\rm PS}^{*}\approx11.8\!-\!12.0,
\qquad W^{*}\approx22.5\!-\!22.9, $$

about $W^{*}\simeq22.6$ with the $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$ root.
In closed form

$$W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
        \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq,
\qquad\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},$$

the familiar $ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ total
Marshallian surplus at the competitive equilibrium.  With the
textbook zero-price normalisation ${\rm PS}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-
\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ this is the net area between the curves on
the economically feasible interval,
${\rm TW}_{0}= {\rm CS}+{\rm PS}=I_{d}-P^{*}q_{0}-I_{s}\approx
15\!-\!17$, about $15.9$ with the numbers quoted above, the $P^{*}q_{0}
\simeq6.7$ transfer being the usual additive constant.  The $I_{d}-I_{s}
\approx 22\!-\!23$ figure is the un-adjusted $CS+PS$ surplus most often
quoted for the $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$ equilibrium.
public_text.1:
In the inverse notation

$$P_{S}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right),\qquad 
P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2, $$

the competitive equilibrium is the unique real root of

$$f(Q):=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0, $$

$f$ being strictly increasing on $Q>2^{1/3}$.  Numerically

$f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$ and Newton iteration gives

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.69-4.70,\qquad Q^{*}\approx 4.69, $$

$$P^{*}=P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})
      =\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}
      \approx 4.62-4.63 , $$

$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 4.62\times4.69\approx21.6$–$21.7$.

Put
$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}\,dq ,\qquad
I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq ,
$$
with the economically relevant zero price point
$P_{S}(q_{0})=0\iff q_{0}^{3}=3$, $q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44$,
and the mathematical start of the log branch $q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.26$.
With $t=\arctan q$,

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx
3.24\!-\!3.29\times10^{1}, $$

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8,\qquad 
I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 32.46\ {\rm for}\ Q^{*}\approx4.69, $$

so that on the usual Marshallian convention

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.46-21.68\approx10.7\!-\!11.0,$$
about $CS^{*}\approx\$10.8$.

On the admissible supply interval

$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
          \approx 9.7\!-\!10.0,$$
$I_{S}\approx9.87$ for the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root,
and

$$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx21.68-9.87\approx11.8\!-\!12.0.$$

Hence in the textbook $CS+PS$ book–keeping

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
     \approx 32.46-9.87\approx22.5\!-\!22.9,$$

e.g. $W^{*}\simeq22.6$–$22.8$ with $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$,
$CS^{*}\simeq10.8$, $PS^{*}\simeq11.8$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq21.7$.  In
closed form

$$W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
        \int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq,
\qquad 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}} ,$$

the familiar $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{D}-P_{S}]dq$ Marshallian surplus at
the market clearing point.

With the usual zero–price normalisation the $P^{*}q_{0}$ rectangle is
removed,

$$W_{net}=CS^{*}+PS_{net}^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-I_{S}(Q^{*}),$$

$$PS_{net}^{*}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx5.0\!-\!5.3, $$

$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $W_{net}\approx15\!-\!17$, about $15.9$ with the
Simpson numbers quoted above.  The $ \approx22\!-\!23$ figure is the
un-normalised $I_{D}-I_{S}$ Marshallian surplus and the $\approx 16$
figure is the same surplus with the $P^{*}q_{0}$ transfer removed.  The
equilibrium $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ is stable under both
normalisations.
public_text.21:
I agree with the market clearing root that the group has converged on

$$P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*}),\qquad 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}} $$

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.62\!-\!4.64 $$

and the numerical integrals are stable on that root,

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5,$$
$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9,$$

with $Q_{0}$ the economic zero-price choke of the inverse supply.

The subtle point is the origin of producer surplus.  $P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is real for $q>\root3\of2$ but it is economically negative for
$\root3\of2<q<\root3\of3$,

$$P_{S}(q)=0\iff q^{3}-2=1\iff Q_{0}=\root3\of3\approx1.442 .$$

Producer surplus is the area under the market price and above the
marginal cost curve on the actually producible part of the schedule,
i.e.

$$PS(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
        =P^{*}\big(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\big)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq ,$$

and

$$CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}.$$

Hence on the economically feasible domain

$$W^{*} =CS+PS
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq .$$

The $P^{*}Q_{0}$ rectangle is the transfer that is normally removed
when surplus is written as the net area between the two curves.  With
$Q_{0}=\root3\of3$,

$$P^{*}Q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66,$$

$$CS\approx I_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.8,$$
$$PS\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-I_{S}\approx4.62\times3.25-9.9\approx5.1,$$

so that

$$W^{*}=CS+PS\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-P^{*}Q_{0}-I_{S}
      \approx32.5-6.7-9.9\approx15.9, $$

about $15\!-\!17$ monetary units, $CS\approx10.8$ and $PS\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$
on the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ equilibrium.  This is the
usual net area between $P_{D}$ and $P_{S}$ on the feasible interval
$Q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$ and the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ term is the conventional
book-keeping correction that removes the artificial surplus generated
on the $0\to Q_{0}$ part of the supply schedule where the inverse supply

The inverse schedules are

$$P_{s}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right),\qquad 
P_{d}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2 , $$

and on the competitive market

$$P_{s}(Q^{*})=P_{d}(Q^{*})\iff 
f(Q):=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0 , $$

$f$ is strictly increasing on $Q>\root3\!\of2$.  Numerically

* $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$,
* $Q^{*}=4.68\!-\!4.70$,

in practice

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}
      \simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7\approx 4.62 ,
$$

$P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq 21.6\!-\!21.7$.  On the usual Marshallian
normalisation

\begin{equation*}
CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq,
\end{equation*}

$Q_{0}=\root3\!\of3$ being the economic zero of the log supply,
$P_{s}(Q_{0})=0$, so that with the admissible mathematical lower
limit $q_{a}=\root3\!\of2$

\begin{equation*}
I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
          \approx 3.24\!-\!3.29\times10^{1}\approx 32.5 ,
\end{equation*}

and, with the elementary anti-derivative of $\ln(q^{3}-2)$,

\begin{equation*}
I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
          \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 9.7 ,
\end{equation*}

on the usual $q_{a}=\root3\!\of2$ domain.  Hence on the textbook
$CS+PS$ bookkeeping

* $CS^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!11.0$,
  $\approx10.8$,
* $PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}\approx 21.7-9.7\approx 11.8\!-\!12.0$,

and

\begin{equation*}
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-
      \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
     \approx 32.5-9.7\approx 2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1},
\end{equation*}

i.e. $W^{*}\simeq22\!-\!23$ welfare units, $W^{*}\approx22.6\!-\!22.9$
for the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root, the familiar
$CS\approx\$10.8$, $PS\approx\$11.8$ decomposition with $P^{*}Q^{*}
\approx\$21.7$ of gross trade value.

With the strict economic zero-price normalisation
$P_{s}(Q_{0})=0$, $Q_{0}=\root3\!\of3\approx1.44$,

$$PS_{e}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s},
\qquad 
W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}
    =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dq-P^{*}Q_{0}
     -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq ,$$

which removes the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.7$ transfer.  Numerically

$\displaystyle\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}\approx9.8\!-\!10.0$,

$PS_{e}\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$ and

$W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}\approx10.8+5.1\approx15\!-\!17$, about
$W_{e}\simeq15.9$ with $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, the
$ \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}[P_{d}-P_{s}]dq\approx7.3\!-\!7.5$ net area
between the two curves on the economically feasible interval
$Q_{0}\le Q\le Q^{*}$.  This is the $CS\approx10.8$, $PS\approx5.1$,
$W\approx15\!-\!16$ zero-price normalisation quoted in Colleagues 1,
11, 19.  Up to the $P^{*}Q_{0}$ transfer this is the $W^{*}\approx
22\!-\!23$ $CS+PS$ value above.

The inverse schedules can be written on the admissible branch

$P_{s}(q)=\ln \!\big(q^{3}-2\big) ,\qquad q>q_{a},\qquad 
q_{a}=2^{1/3}$,
$P_{d}(q)=18\,e^{-\arctan q}$ ,
$P_{s}(q)$ is strictly increasing on $q>q_{a}$ and $P_{d}$ is strictly
decreasing, so that

\begin{equation*}
P_{s}(Q^{*})=P_{d}(Q^{*}),\qquad 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}} ,
\end{equation*}
has a unique real root on $q>q_{a}$.  On $4<Q<5$

$f(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ changes sign
between $4.68$ and $4.70$ and

\begin{equation*}
Q^{*}\approx 4.69\!-\!4.70,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx
4.6\!-\!4.7,
\end{equation*}
e.g. $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq21.6\!-\!21.7$,
is the competitive price quantity pair.  In the $u=\arctan q$
variable

$I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq
   =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du$, $u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}$,
so that numerically

$I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx
3.24\!-\!3.29\times10^{1}\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8$,

say $I_{d}\approx 32.5$.  On the admissible supply branch

$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq$,
$q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.26$, is finite and

$I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx9.7\!-\!9.9$,

e.g. $I_{s}\approx9.70$ for $Q^{*}\approx4.69$.  With the usual
Marshallian accounting

$CS^{*}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}$,
$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}(Q^{*})$,

hence

$CS^{*}\approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!11.0\approx \$10.8$,

$PS^{*}\approx 21.7-9.7\approx 11.8\!-\!12.0\approx \$12.0$,

and the net $CS+PS$ surplus on the admissible branch is

\begin{equation*}
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-
      \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq\approx 22\!-\!23,
\end{equation*}
about $W^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$ with the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$ root, e.g. $W^{*}\approx22.8$, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$,
$PS^{*}\approx12.0$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.  This is the
$I_{d}-I_{s}$ total surplus $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{d}-P_{s}]_{+}dq$
normally quoted as the competitive total welfare.

Remark.  If the producer surplus is normalised to the economic
zero-price point $P_{s}(Q_{0})=0$, $Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx
1.442$, the economically relevant producer surplus is
$PS_{0}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$
and

$W_{0}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}
      -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq\approx15\!-\!17$,

about $W_{0}\simeq15.9$, $CS^{*}\simeq10.8$, $PS_{0}\simeq5.1$,
the textbook $CS+PS$ with the $P_{s}=0$ origin.  The $\approx6\!-\!7$
difference between $W^{*}$ and $W_{0}$ is the $P^{*}Q_{0}
+\int_{q_{a}}^{Q_{0}}P_{s}dq$ shift between the mathematical domain
normalisation $q_{a}=2^{1/3}$ and the economic zero-price
normalisation $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$.  The equilibrium $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$ is robust under either convention.
public_text.12:
The market clearing price is the unique real solution of

$$P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff 
\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv f(Q)=0,\qquad 
Q^{3}>2 ,$$

$f$ is strictly monotone on $Q>\root3\of2$ and

* $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$,

so that on the usual numerical accuracy

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69 ,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7, $$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.689$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ and $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$.
Put $Q_{0}$ for the economic zero of the inverse supply,
$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=\root3\of3\approx1.442$, and
on the admissible branch $q\ge Q_{0}$

$$ 
{\rm CS}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},
\qquad 
{\rm PS}(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq ,
$$

so that with the inessential $P^{*}Q_{0}$ cancellation

$$ 
W(Q^{*})={\rm CS}+{\rm PS}
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
       =I_{d}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*}) .
$$

In the $u=\arctan q$ variable

$$I_{d}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
           =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du ,$$

and with the root above

$$I_{d}(Q^{*})\approx 3.24\!-\!3.29\times10^{1}\approx32.4\!-\!32.8,
\qquad I_{d}\approx32.5,$$

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.7,$$
hence

$${\rm CS}^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8,$$

and

$$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
          \approx9.8\!-\!9.9\approx9.9, $$

so that on the conventional $0\to Q^{*}$ Marshallian convention

$${\rm PS}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8\!-\!12.0,$$

and

$$W^{*}= {\rm CS}^{*}+{\rm PS}^{*}=I_{d}-I_{s}
      \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23, $$

e.g. $W^{*}\approx22.6$ with $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,
${\rm CS}^{*}\approx10.8$, ${\rm PS}^{*}\approx11.8$ and $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.
With the coarse Simpson rule used in the discussion this is the
$W^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$ total Marshallian surplus,
$I_{d}\approx32.5$ gross willingness to pay, generated at the
$Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$ competitive equilibrium.

Remark on normalisation.  On the textbook zero-price normalisation

$${\rm PS}_{0}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S},
\qquad 
W_{0}={\rm CS}+{\rm PS}_{0}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq,
$$

so that $ {\rm PS}_{0}\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$ and
$W_{0}\approx15\!-\!17$, about $W_{0}\approx15.9$ with the same
$Q^{*},P^{*}$, i.e. the $CS\approx10.8$, $PS_{0}\approx5.1$,
$W_{0}\approx15.9$ figure often quoted as the between-the-curves
net surplus.  The $I_{d}-I_{s}\approx22\!-\!23$ number above is the
$CS+PS$ surplus with the usual $P^{*}Q^{*}$ cancellation.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the numerical core that is now settled in the room.

P_S(Q)=ln(Q³-2), P_D(Q)=18 e^{-arctan Q}, P_S(Q*)=P_D(Q*) gives

ln(Q*³-2)=18 e^{-arctan Q*}, f strictly increasing for Q>2^{1/3}.

f(4.68)<0<f(4.70) and Newton gives

Q*≈4.69–4.70, Q*≈4.69, 
P* = ln(Q*³-2)=18 e^{-arctan Q*}≈4.62–4.64, P*≈4.62,
P*Q*≈21.6–21.7.

Demand integral is stable

I_D(Q*)=∫_0^{Q*}18 e^{-arctan q}dq
      =18∫_0^{arctan Q*}e^{-t} sec²t dt
≈32.4–32.8, ≈32.46 for Q*≈4.69.

Hence
CS* = I_D - P*Q* ≈32.46-21.68≈10.7–11.0≈10.8
is common to everyone.

The only remaining accounting issue is the origin of producer surplus.
P_S(q)=ln(q³-2) is real for q>2^{1/3} but it is economically negative for
2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}. The economic choke is

P_S(q0)=0 ⇔ q0³-2=1 ⇔ q0=∛3≈1.442,

whereas q_a=∛2≈1.260 is only the mathematical branch point of the log.
Production does not occur at negative inverse marginal cost, so the textbook
Marshallian producer surplus is measured from the zero-price point:

PS* = ∫_{q0}^{Q*} [P* - P_S(q)] dq
    = P*(Q* - q0) - ∫_{q0}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq .

With the settled root

∫_{q0}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq ≈9.8–9.9,
P*(Q* - q0)≈4.62×(4.69-1.442)≈15.0,

so
PS*≈15.0-9.9≈5.0–5.3, ≈5.1 on the usual Simpson mesh.

Total Marshallian surplus on the economically feasible interval is therefore

W* = CS* + PS*
   = I_D(Q*) - P*Q0 - ∫_{q0}^{Q*} P_S(q)dq
   = ∫_0^{Q*} P_D dq - P*q0 - ∫_{q0}^{Q*} P_S dq
≈32.5 - 6.66 - 9.87
≈15–17, ≈15.9 with Q*≈4.69, P*≈4.62, CS*≈10.8, PS*≈5.1.

That is the net area actually created between demand and the non-negative part
of marginal cost on q0≤q≤Q*. The ≈22–23 numbers that appear as I_D - ∫_{q_a}^{Q*} P_S
are W* + P*q0. They keep the P*q0≈6.6–6.7 transfer in the total and, if the
supply integral is started at q_a=∛2, they also integrate over the region
q_a<q<q0 where P_S<0. Removing the inessential transfer and the negative-price
tail gives the conventional CS+PS total of order ~16 at the Q*≈4.69, P*≈4.62
competitive equilibrium.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think we are essentially all on the same mechanical numbers now and that is helpful.

Clearing is
$P_S(Q^*)=P_D(Q^*)\iff \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^*}$,
$f$ monotone for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and
$f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$
so that
$Q^*\approx4.69-4.70$, $Q^*\simeq4.69$,
$P^*=\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^*}\simeq4.62-4.64$,
$P^*Q^*\simeq21.6-21.7$.
With $t=\arctan q$
$I_D(Q^*)=\int_0^{Q^*}18e^{-\arctan q}dq=18\int_0^{\arctan Q^*}e^{-t}\sec^2t\,dt\approx32.4-32.6$,
about $32.5$ on the usual Simpson mesh, so that
$CS^*=I_D-P^*Q^*\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7-11.0$, essentially the $CS\approx10.8$ everyone is quoting. That part is settled.

The remaining book-keeping question is where producer surplus is measured from. 
$P_S(q)=\ln(q^3-2)$ is $ <0$ on $2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$ and
$P_S(q)=0\iff q^3-2=1\iff Q_0=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442$.
$q_a=2^{1/3}\simeq1.26$ is only the mathematical branch point of the log; it is not an economic choke point. Production is not meaningful for $P_S<0$.

Textbook Marshallian producer surplus is therefore
$PS(Q^*)=\int_{Q_0}^{Q^*}[P^*-P_S(q)]dq
       =P^*(Q^*-Q_0)-\int_{Q_0}^{Q^*} \ln(q^3-2)dq$,
and
$W^*=CS^*+PS^*
    =\int_0^{Q^*}P_D(q)dq-P^*Q_0-\int_{Q_0}^{Q^*}P_S(q)dq$.

Numerically
$\int_{Q_0}^{Q^*}\ln(q^3-2)dq\approx9.8-9.9$,
$P^*Q_0\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66$,
$P^*(Q^*-Q_0)\approx4.62\times3.25\approx15.0$,
so
$PS^*\approx15.0-9.9\approx5.0-5.3$, about $5.1$ on the $Q^*\simeq4.69$, $P^*\simeq4.62$ root,
and
$W^*=CS^*+PS^*\approx10.8+5.1\approx15-17$,
$W^*\simeq15.9$ with the Simpson numbers usually quoted,
$CS\simeq10.8$, $PS_{\rm net}\simeq5.1$, $Q^*\simeq4.69$, $P^*\simeq4.62$.

The $I_D-I_S\approx32.5-9.7\approx22-23$ numbers that appear in the literature are
$W^*+P^*Q_0$, i.e. $CS+PS$ with the $P^*Q_0\approx6.7$ transfer kept inside the producer integral and with the supply integral started at the mathematical point $q_a=2^{1/3}$ where $P_S<0$. Once producer surplus is measured from the economic zero-price choke $P_S=0$ at $Q_0=3^{1/3}$ the transfer is removed and the net area actually created between demand and marginal cost on the feasible interval $Q_0\le q\le Q^*$ is the $\sim15-16$ total that is the conventional $CS+PS$ welfare.

That is the zero-price normalised total most of us were originally after, and it is consistent with the agreed $Q^*,P^*,CS$ numbers.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the numbers on the equilibrium itself and think we can all settle them now.

The clearing condition
$ \ln(Q^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q} $
is monotone on $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.62\!-\!4.64$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$,

is robust.  $I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.4\!-\!32.8$, about $32.5$, so
$CS^{*}=I_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx\$10.8$
is essentially common.

The remaining accounting issue is where producer surplus is measured from.  
$P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is real for $q>2^{1/3}$ but economically meaningful only where price is non-negative.
$P_{S}(q)=0\iff q^{3}-2=1\iff q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$,
whereas $q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.26$ is only the mathematical branch point.  
On $q_{a}<q<q_{0}$ we have $P_{S}<0$, i.e. the inverse supply is negative.

Textbook producer surplus is
$PS^{*}= \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$,
and consumer surplus is the usual
$CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$.

Hence the net surplus created by trade is
$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq$.

Numerically
$\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9$,
$P^{*}q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66\!-\!6.70$,
so
$PS^{*}\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-9.85\approx4.62\times3.25-9.85\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$,
$CS^{*}\approx10.7\!-\!10.9$,
and
$W^{*}\approx32.5-6.66-9.85\approx15\!-\!17$, about $15.9$ with the Simpson numbers we are all using, i.e. $CS\approx10.8$, $PS\approx5.1$, $W\approx15.9$.

The $\approx22\!-\!23$ figure that appears as $I_{D}-I_{S}$ with $I_{S}=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ is $W^{*}+P^{*}q_{0}$.  It keeps the $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.7$ rectangle in the total and measures producer surplus on the mathematical domain where $P_{S}<0$ on $q_{a}<q<q_{0}$.  Once the surplus is measured from the economic zero-price choke $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ the inessential transfer is removed and the conventional $CS+PS$ net welfare at the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ competitive equilibrium is the $\sim15\!-\!16$ net area between demand and the economically feasible part of supply, essentially the $\approx15.9$ value quoted above.

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
       \approx 32.4\!-\!32.8\approx 32.5 ,$$

and

$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq
       \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 9.7 , $$

so that on the usual $0\to Q^{*}$ Marshallian book–keeping

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}
      \approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!11.0\approx \$10.8,$$

$$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})
      \approx 21.7-9.7\approx 11.8\!-\!12.2\approx \$12.0,$$

and

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-
      \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
     \approx 32.5-9.7\approx 22\!-\!23 ,
$$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,

$I_{D}\approx32.46$, $I_{S}\approx9.70$,

$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS^{*}\approx11.8\!-\!12.0$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$ and

$$W^{*}\approx 22.6\!-\!22.9\approx 22.8 $$

in the $CS+PS=I_{D}-I_{S}$ normalisation.  In closed form

$$W^{*}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
       \int_{2^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq,
\qquad \ln\!\big(Q^{*3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}.$$

Remark. With the economic zero-price choke $P_{S}(Q_{0})=0$,
$Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$, the textbook net surplus is

$PS_{0}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$,
$W_{0}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}=I_{D}-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}
      \approx15\!-\!17$,

$PS_{0}\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $W_{0}\approx15.9$
with the same $Q^{*}\! \approx\!4.69$, $P^{*}\!\approx\!4.62$, i.e.
$W^{*}=W_{0}+P^{*}Q_{0}$ with $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.66$.  The $22\!-\!23$
figure above is the un-normalised $I_{D}-I_{S}$ Marshallian total
surplus most of the group is quoting for the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$ competitive equilibrium.

8.text:
The inverse equilibrium is

$P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff 
\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv f(Q)=0 ,\; Q>\sqrt[3]{2} $

$f'>0$ on the admissible branch and $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$, so that
with Newton/bisection

* $Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
* $P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}
      \simeq4.62\!-\!4.64$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,

$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$.  With $t=\arctan q$

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
          =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
          \approx 32.4\!-\!32.9\approx32.5 .
$$

Hence on the usual Marshallian convention

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}
      \approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx \$10.8,
$$

which is settled.

For an inverse supply the economic origin is $P_{S}(Q_{0})=0$.
$P_{S}(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$,

$$
Q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}\approx1.442,
 $$

whereas $\,q_{a}=\sqrt[3]{2}\approx1.26$ is the mathematical branch
point of the log.  On the economically feasible interval $Q_{0}\le q\le
Q^{*}$

$$
PS_{e}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
            =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
              \ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq ,
$$

$$
\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9,
\qquad 
P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)\approx4.62\times3.25\approx15.0,
$$

so that

$$
PS_{e}\approx15.0-9.85\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx \$5.1 ,
$$

and the net Marshallian surplus measured from the zero price choke is

$$
W_{e}=CS^{*}+PS_{e}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q_{0}
      -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
     =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-I_{S}^{0}(Q^{*}),
$$

$$
W_{e}\approx32.5-4.62\times1.442-9.85
      \approx32.5-6.66-9.85\approx15\!-\!17,
$$

about

$$
W_{e}\simeq15.9,\qquad CS^{*}\simeq10.8,\qquad PS_{e}\simeq5.1,
$$

for $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, i.e. the $\sim 16$ units of net
area between $P_{D}$ and $P_{S}$ on the feasible interval
$Q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$.  This is the textbook $CS+PS$ net welfare,
$CS\approx10.8$ plus the genuine producer surplus $\approx5.1$.

Remark.  With the purely mathematical lower limit $q_{a}=\sqrt[3]{2}$ the
un-normalised $CS+PS$ book-keeping is

$$
W^{a}=CS^{*}+PS^{a}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-
      \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
      \approx32.5-9.7\approx22\!-\!23,
$$

e.g. $PS^{a}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}^{a}\approx11.8\!-\!12.2$, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$
and $W^{a}\approx22.6\!-\!22.9$, $W^{a}\approx22.8$ for
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.  $W^{a}=W_{e}+P^{*}Q_{0}$,
$P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.6\!-\!6.7$, the inessential $P^{*}Q_{0}$ transfer
which is normally removed in the zero-price normalisation above.

19.text:
The clearing point is essentially settled.

$P_{S}(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2),\;P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q},\;Q^{3}>2$

$$

20.text:
The inverse schedules

$P_{S}(Q)=\ln\big(Q^{3}-2\big),\qquad P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2$

give on the admissible branch the unique competitive root of

$f(Q)=\ln\big(Q^{3}-2\big)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0$ .

$f$ is strictly increasing for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$,

so that with the usual Newton/bisection

$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69$
$P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.62\!-\!4.64$
$P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq4.62\times4.69\simeq21.6\!-\!21.7$

is now common to the whole group.  With $t=\arctan q$

$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
           =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
           \approx 32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.5$

so that on the conventional Marshallian definition

$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\simeq10.8$

is settled.

The only remaining book-keeping issue is the lower limit of the producer
integral.  $P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is real for $q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.26$ but
it is economically meaningful only for $P_{S}\ge0$,

$P_{S}(q_{0})=0\iff q_{0}^{3}-2=1\iff q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$,

the economic zero-price choke of the inverse supply.  On the feasible
interval $q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$ the textbook producer surplus is

$PS_{0}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
            =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-q_{0}\right)-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
              \ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq,$

and

$W_{0}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}q_{0}
      -\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq .$

Numerically

$\displaystyle\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9$,
$P^{*}q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66$,

hence

$PS_{0}\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-9.9\approx4.62\times3.25-9.9
       \approx5.0\!-\!5.3\simeq5.1$,

$CS^{*}\simeq10.8$,

$W_{0}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}\approx I_{D}-P^{*}q_{0}-I_{S}(q_{0})
     \approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!17$,

about $W_{0}\simeq15.9$ for $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$,
$CS\simeq10.8$, $PS_{0}\simeq5.1$.

This is the net area between demand and marginal cost on the
economically feasible interval $Q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$, i.e. the usual
$CS+PS$ total with producer surplus measured from the zero-price choke.

Removing the $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.7$ transfer the formal $I_{D}-I_{S}$
gross surplus on the mathematical domain $q_{a}=2^{1/3}$ is

$W^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
     \approx32.5-9.7\approx22\!-\!23$,

$W^{*}\simeq22.6\!-\!22.9$, $CS^{*}\simeq10.8$, $PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}
\simeq11.8\!-\!12.0$, the $W^{*} = W_{0}+P^{*}q_{0}$ number quoted by
Colleagues 10,12,14,15,18,20,21.  Up to the inessential $P^{*}q_{0}$
transfer it is the same equilibrium, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,

being the conventionally reported $CS+PS$ total.

10.text:
The inverse schedules are on the admissible branch

$P_{S}(Q)=\ln (Q^{3}-2),\;Q^{3}>2,\qquad P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$,

$I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6\!-\!9.7$,

I_{S}^{a}\approx9.7$ gives

$$f(Q)=\ln (Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0 , \qquad Q>2^{1/3} .$$

      4.62\!-\!4.64\approx 4.62 , $$

          =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx

$0\to Q^{*}$ Marshallian book-keeping

11.8\!-\!12.2\approx\$12.0 ,$$

      \approx 32.5-9.7\approx22\!-\!23,$$

e.g. $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$,

$I_{D}\simeq32.5$, $I_{S}^{a}\simeq9.70$,
$CS^{*}\simeq10.8$, $PS^{*}\simeq12.0$, $W^{g}\simeq22.6\!-\!22.9$,

of gross value of trade being split $\approx10.8$ consumer and
$\approx12.0$ producer surplus.  In closed form

$$W^{g}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
       \int_{2^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq,
\qquad \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}} .$$

$W_{0}^{*}\simeq15.9$ for the $Q^{*}\!\approx\!4.69,\;P^{*}\!\approx\!4.62$
root, i.e. $CS^{*}\simeq10.8$, $PS_{0}^{*}\simeq5.1$, $W_{0}^{*}\simeq16$

Remark.  With the purely mathematical lower limit $q_{a}=2^{1/3}$,

the un-normalised Marshallian sum

       \approx32.5-9.7\approx22\!-\!23,

is the $I_{D}-I_{S}$ gross surplus most of the group quotes; the

16.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the mechanical part is now essentially settled in the room and I will take the numbers everyone is converging on.

$P_{S}(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2),\;P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$

$P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})\iff \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$

is monotone for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.62\!-\!4.64$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$.

With $t=\arctan q$

$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
            =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
            \approx32.4\!-\!32.8$, $\approx32.5$ on the usual mesh,
so

$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0$,

about $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, which is unassailable.

The only substantive issue left is where producer surplus is measured from. $P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is mathematically real for $q>2^{1/3}$ but it is economically negative for $2^{1/3}<q<3^{1/3}$.

$P_{S}(q)=0\iff q^{3}-2=1\iff q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$,

while $q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$ is only the log branch point. On $q_{a}<q<q_{0}$ the inverse supply is negative, i.e. a price at which the firm would be paid to produce. Producer surplus is conventionally

$PS(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
        =P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$,

and not $P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$.
Consumer surplus is as above,

$CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$.

Hence the textbook net welfare is

$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}q_{0}
      -\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$,

i.e. demand up to $Q^{*}$ minus the economic area under marginal cost up to $Q^{*}$ with the fixed transfer $P^{*}q_{0}$ removed.

Numerically

$\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9$,

$P^{*}q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66\!-\!6.70$,

so that

$PS^{*}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}
      \approx4.62\times(4.69-1.44)-9.85\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$,

about $PS^{*}\approx5.1$, and

$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     \approx32.5-6.66-9.85\approx15\!-\!17$,

$\approx15.9$ with the $Q^{*}\approx4.69,\;P^{*}\approx4.62$ root, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS^{*}\approx5.1$.

The $I_{D}-I_{S}\approx22\!-\!23$ figures are $I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$, i.e. $CS^{*}+PS^{*}+P^{*}q_{0}$. They keep the $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.7$ rectangle in the total. That is the gross $I_{D}-I_{S}$ Marshallian surplus, not the conventional net $CS+PS$ measured from the zero-price choke $P_{S}=0$.

Even with the refined demand quadrature that colleague 14 reports, $I_{D}\approx32.81$, the net correction is unchanged: $W_{net}=I_{D}-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx32.81-6.68-9.85\approx16.3$, still in the $\sim15\!-\!17$ net-surplus basin. The numerical sensitivity of the upper tail of $\int e^{-\arctan q}$ does not remove the $P^{*}q_{0}$ transfer.

In closed form the conventional net total surplus at the competitive equilibrium is

$W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
       -P^{*}3^{1/3}
       -\int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$,

$\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$,

which with the room’s $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ gives $CS\approx10.8$, $PS\approx5.1$ and $W^{*}\approx15.9$, the usual between-the-curves net welfare on the economically feasible interval $q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$.

           =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t dt
           \approx 32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.5\!-\!32.8$,

so that

$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.1$
$\approx \$10.8$,

essentially invariant.

The only book-keeping left is the lower limit of the producer integral.
$P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is real for $q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$ but
economically non-negative only for

$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff\ln(Q_{0}^{3}-2)=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$,

On the feasible interval $Q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$

$\displaystyle I_{S}^{0}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
       \approx9.8\!-\!9.9$,

$P^{*}Q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66$,

$PS_{0}^{*}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-I_{S}^{0}(Q^{*})
          \approx4.62(4.69-1.442)-9.87\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx\$5.1$,

and the textbook net Marshallian surplus measured from the zero price choke

$W_{0}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}^{*}
       = I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-I_{S}^{0}(Q^{*})$
$\approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!17$,

$W_{0}^{*}\simeq15.9$, $CS^{*}\simeq10.8$, $PS_{0}^{*}\simeq5.1$ for

area between demand and the non-negative part of marginal cost on
$Q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$.

In closed form

$W_{0}^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
        -P^{*}3^{1/3}
        -\int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$,

Remark.  On the purely mathematical normalisation
$I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6\!-\!9.7$
the un-shifted $I_{D}-I_{S}$ Marshallian sum is

$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{a*}
        =I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx32.5-9.7\approx22\!-\!23$,

$PS^{a*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}^{a}\approx11.8\!-\!12.2$, $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6\!-\!22.9$
$\approx22.8$ for the same $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root,

number is the $W_{0}\approx15.9$ net total with the inessential

19.text:
The clearing point is now mechanical.

* $P_{S}(Q)=\ln (Q^{3}-2),\;P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$

           =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt

on a $0.25$ mesh close-out.  Hence

$CS^{*}\approx\$10.8$,
essentially invariant.

          \ln(q^{3}-2)dq$,

        =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
        \approx32.5-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!17$,

$W_{0}^{*}\simeq15.9$ for $Q^{*}\approx4.69,\;P^{*}\approx4.62$,
$CS^{*}\simeq10.8$, $PS_{0}^{*}\simeq5.1$.
With the refined demand quadrature $I_{D}\approx32.81$ this is
$W_{0}^{*}\approx16.2\!-\!16.3$.

This is the net area actually created between demand and the non-negative
part of marginal cost on $Q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$.
The $I_{D}-I_{S}$ Marshallian sum with the mathematical lower limit
$q_{a}=2^{1/3}$,

$I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6\!-\!9.9$,

transfer retained in the integral.  Removing the transfer gives the
conventional net welfare $\approx\$15\!-\!17$, $ \approx\$15.9$

      = P*(Q* - q0) - ∫_{q0}^{Q*} ln(q^3-2) dq,

     = I_D(Q*) - P* q0 - ∫_{q0}^{Q*} P_S(q) dq,
i.e. willingness to pay up to Q* minus the economic area under marginal cost on the feasible interval, with the fixed infra-marginal transfer P* q0 removed.
